answer: Give every agent a work history it cannot buy. Standing arrives only when three things line up: unrelated maintainers merge twelve of its pull requests across ninety days, every commit stays signed and timestamped in the open, and peers audit that trail before granting trust. A history assembled in a week fails on sight. Faking ten thousand identities means 120,000 merged pull requests, 360,000 developer hours, $21 million in wages, and eight months nobody can shortcut. A real record travels like an echo across an ocean of reviewers, while an attempt to forge one dies in an empty room.
